content.text:
Fair question — here's the real picture, not spin.

**16 phases of engine/backend code are built** (packages/*): Core (DI, event bus, scheduler), Storage (VFS/IndexedDB/OPFS), Layer, Timeline, Animation, Rendering (WebGPU/WebGL2/Canvas2D), Effects, Audio, Export, History (undo/redo), Assets, AI (TTS via Kokoro/Piper), Plugin system. All of that has unit test coverage and mostly works at the code level.

**But the actual UI (`apps/studio`) only wires 8 of those 13 engines** — Audio, Export, AI, and Effects were explicitly deferred in Phase 15 and never got panels. So what you can actually click around and see in the browser right now is:

- 5 panels (Viewport, Timeline, Layers, Properties, Toolbar)
- Import a video asset
- Move/drag a clip on the timeline
- Undo/redo

**That's it.** No Trim UI. No Export button. No way to add a Text layer (everything is asset-driven). No AI/TTS panel. No effects panel. There's also a known bug where clicking Undo in the toolbar immediately after a drag is a no-op (dnd-kit swallows the click) — `Mod+Z` works around it.

So: a lot of engine work, very little of it is exposed through the actual UI yet. If the expectation was a usable editor demo, that's not where this is — it's still mostly plumbing with a thin, partial UI on top. If you want, I can pull up `docs/24-roadmap/mvp.md` or `PLAN.md` to show what's still queued to wire into the UI.

Every layer renders at a fixed `PLACEHOLDER_BOUNDS` (200×200) — no engine models a Layer's intrinsic size yet.

### 15.3 Timeline panel

- [x] Virtualized track/clip view (only render visible clips) — **scoped down to plain full render, no windowing**; track/item counts in this vertical slice are small enough that virtualization has no observable benefit yet
- [x] Playhead scrubbing — click-to-seek on track lane background, via `PlaybackService`

- [x] Snapping indicators — **not implemented**

- [x] Thin UI view over `AssetManager` (no registry of its own — ADR-002) — `AssetEditorService` is a pure passthrough
- [x] Import button (opens File System Access API picker) — plain `<input type=file multiple>`, not the File System Access API (broader browser support, same user-facing result for import)
